INDUSTRIAL DESIGNS REGULATIONS, 1984
1984/83.
2006-2.
Authority: These Regulations were made on 17th April, 1984 by the Minister under
section 49 of the Industrial Designs Act.
Commencement: 17th April, 1984.
Citation
1. These Regulations may be cited as the Industrial Designs
Short title.
Regulations, 1984.
Interpretation
2. In these Regulations,
Definitions.
(a) "applicant" means a person for whom an application is made;
.
(b) "application" means an application for registration of an
industrial design;
(c) "Office" means the Industrial Property Office.
Fees
3. The fees to be paid under the Act and these Regulations are Fees set out.
those fixed in Schedule I. Schedule I.
4. Payments shall be made in Barbadian currency, but the
Currency.
equivalent amount in a foreign currency that is convertible in
Barbados may be accepted.

5. When a fee paid by a person to the Director for any purpose
Excess fee.
exceeds the fee fixed by these Regulations for that purpose by more
than $10, the person who paid the fee is entitled to be refunded the
amount of excess less $10.
6. When a fee is paid to the Director by any person by mistake for
Fee refund.
an application that is withdrawn before it is given an application
number, or for a service that cannot be provided, the person who paid
the fee is entitled to a refund of the fee less $25, if he claims the refund
within one year of the payment of the fee.
7. When a person pays a fee in advance for registration, he is
Refund of
advance fee. entitled to a refund of the fee, less $15, if the application is withdrawn.
8. (1) Fees that are paid by cheque, bank draft or money order
Payment of
fees. shall be forwarded to the Director and made payable to him.
(2) Fees may be paid by cash at the Office.
9. A payment of a fee by cheque may be accepted by the Director
Cheques.
as being a payment of the fee when the cheque is received by him, but
if the cheque is not paid when presented to the bank on which it is
drawn and not made good within such time as the Director may fix,
the acceptance of the fee is revoked and any thing done pursuant to the
payment is void and, if appropriate, shall be so recorded in the
register.
Forms
10. (1) In submitting a document to the Office for any purpose,
Form
required. the person submitting the document must use the form set out in
Schedule II that is appropriate for the purpose, but the form may be
Schedule II.
modified in such manner as is necessary in the circumstances.
(2) In submitting a document to the Office, one copy only of the
document need be submitted.
11. If a document that is submitted to the Office differs
Replacing
documents. significantly from the form in Schedule II intended to be used for
the purpose of the submission, the Director may require that the

A 3 L.R.O. 1989 Industrial Designs CAP. 309A
Regulations, 1984 regs. 12-15
document be replaced, within a time fixed by the Director, by one
that conforms to the document required by Schedule II to be used
for the purpose.
12. (1) All applications, notices, statements, papers having paper
representations affixed, or other documents authorised or required =qh-
by the Act or these regulations to be made, left or sent to the ments.
Director must be on strong, durable white paper and, except in the
case of statutory documents and affidavits, must be written on 1
side of the paper only.
(2) Each sheet not being a graphic representation must have its
short sides at the top and bottom.
(3) Each sheet must be of the same size and on A-4 paper or
such other size as the Director may permit.
13. (1) The pages of documents, other than graphic Page
representations must be numbered consecutively, preferably at the ;;z-
top of the page.
(2) Page margins must be not less than 2 cm.
(3) Except for graphic representations, pages must be typed or
printed, preferably with 1 */z spacing or double spacing.
14. (1) An application must be in English. Language of
(2) Until he is provided with a translation verified by affidavit, doc”ments’
the Director may refuse to take cognisance of any document that
is not in English.
Photographs, Drawings and Specimens
15. The graphic representations in an application must meet ~r.+k~re-
the following reqirements: quirements.
(a) the representations are to be on white paper or other
material suitable for reproduction;
(b) the sheets of representations are to be ‘he same size as
those used in the application;
(c) the representations are to be prepared in durable dark lines
I
suitable for reproduction;
(d) the representations are to appear on only 1 side of a sheet;

(e) the representations are to be on a scale sufficiently large to
show the features of the design clearly;
cf) figures in a representation are to be numbered
consecutively without regard to the number of sheets in
the representation and so far as possible the figures are to
be arranged in numerical order; and
(g) figures in a representation can be continued on subsequent
sheets if necessary or several figures can appear on the
same page.
Folds, 16. Graphic representations in an application must be free of
breaks. such folds, breaks or creases as render them unsuitable for
reproduction.
17. Photographs of an article taken against a neutral
PhOtO-
graphs. background may be used in an application instead of graphic
representations if the photographs clearly illustrate the design and
can be readily reproduced.
18. (1) The Director may require that a graphic representation
Rules about
specimens. or a photograph be provided instead of a specimen when the size
and weight of the specimen makes it difficult to process and store
it; and, in any event, a specimen must not exceed 1 kilogram in
weight or 30 centimetres in any dimension.
(2) Specimens that are perishable or made of dangerous
material shall not be submitted to the Office.
Correspondence
communi- 19. Applications, correspondence related thereto, and all
cating with communications intended for the Office shall be mailed to or
0fficx.z.
deposited at the Industrial Property Office, Barbados.
Mode of 20. (1) Applications shall be proceeded with, and other
wmmuni- communication with the Office effected, by written
cation.
correspondence; and, unless the Director for good reason decides
otherwise, no regard need be given to any other mode of
communication with the Office.
(2) When communicating with the Office about an application
or registered design, the correspondent shall identify the

A 5 L.R.O. 1989 industrial Designs CAP. 309A
Regulations, 1984 regs. 21-25
application or registration clearly, giving such information as the
date of filing, kind of product, name of applicant and registration
number.
21. All correspondence from the Office to an applicant shall GXIUII~~-
be sent ding from
office.
(a) to the agent of the applicant if an agent resident in
Barbados has been appointed;
(b) if no agent has been appointed in Barbados, to the address
for service of the applicant in Barbados; or
(c) to the applicant, if no agent has been appointed in
Barbados to represent the applicant and the applicant has
no address for service filed in the Office.
22. When, in respect of an application, there is more than 1 MU&AC
applicant, correspondence shall be conducted applicants.
(a) with the applicants’ agent in Barbados if an agent resident
in Barbados has been named to represent all the applicants;
(b) with an applicant resident in Barbados who has been
nominated to represent all the applicants, if no agent
resident in Barbados has been appointed,
(c) with the first applicant named in the application, if there is
neither an agent resident in Barbados nor an applicant
resident in Barbados who has been appointed to represent
the applicants.
23. The Office shall conduct correspondence concerning an Limited=-
application with only 1 person, but having regard to sections 21 =spondau.
and 22.
24. A person who corresponds with the Ofike shall provide Add=smsd
his full postal address, and any correspondence sent by the Office Pxs~Pion.
to that person at the address so provided shall be deemed to be
sent on the date that the records of the Office show it to have been
sent.
25. A licensee and a person who is shown on the register as Addresfsor
the owner of a design must maintain an address for service in S~~CS.
Barbados and provide the Director with notice of that address for
recording in the register.

Time Limits
Filing rime. 26. Any correspondence with the Office that is due on any day
on which the Office is closed for business shall be accepted as
properly filed if it is received on the next day that the Offrce is
open for business.
Replace- 27. If he is satisfied that mail to or from the Office was sent
ment of but never received, the Director may accept or send out replacing
corrrespnl-
correspondence; and the effective date of the replacing
dence.
correspondence is whatever date the Director determines should
apply.
28. Where, by evidence satisfactory to the Director, a person
rntermp-
tials of proves that he was unable to do any thing within the time
mail. prescribed therefor by the Act or these regulations because of an
interruption in mail service in Barbados or elsewhere, the Director
may, before or after the expiration of the time for doing that thing,
extend the time to make allowances for the period of the
interruption in mail service.
Fixing 29. The Director may, in respect of an application, fix a period
rime of time for the doing of any thing for which no time limit is
limits.
otherwise fixed by the Act or these regulations; and an application
shall be deemed abandoned if, in respect of that application, the
thing is not done within the time so fixed.
30. When, by an affidavit setting out the relevant facts, the
(=w+x
time Limits. Director is satisfied that any time fixed by these regulations for
the doing of any thing should be extended in a particular case, the
Director may, either before or after the expiration of the time,
extend it for such period as he thinks suitable in the circumstances
of the case.
Joint Applicants and Owners
31. When an application that is filed by joint applicants is
stricture re
withdrawal. being proceeded with by one of the joint applicants, it may not be
withdrawn without the written permission of all the other joint
applicants.

A7 L.R.O. 2007 Industrial Designs CAP. 309A
Regulations, 1984 regs. 32-37
32. A design registration that is owned by several persons may not
Renouncing
be renounced under section 36 of the Act without the written joint
designs.
permission of all the owners of the design.
Joint Designers
33. When, after an application has been filed, it appears that the
Changes of
names of one or more creators of the design were improperly included designers'
names.
in or omitted from the application, then, if the Director is satisfied, by
an affidavit setting out all the relevant facts, that a correction should
be made, the Director may delete or add, as the case requires, the names
of those other creators.
34. When a design is created by several persons and one or more
Creators not
of them refuses to make an application in respect of the design, or the applying.
whereabouts of one or more of the creators cannot be ascertained after
a diligent inquiry, the other creators may make an application in
respect of that design; and, if the Director is satisfied, by an affidavit
setting out the relevant facts, that the creators missing from the
application either refuse to make application or cannot be located, the
creators making the application are entitled to register the design if all
other requirements of the Act and these Regulations are complied with.
Clerical Errors
35. A document relating to an application or registration may be
Correcting
corrected if the Director is satisfied that the document contains an errors.
error of a clerical nature and that its correction would involve no change
of substance to the application or registration.
General
36. Where no provision is made in the Act or these Regulations in
Providing
respect of any matter arising in the administration of the Act, the for
deficiencies.
Director may make such directions in respect thereof as he considers
necessary.
37. (1) The Director may give a certificate, other than a
Director's
certificate under section 23 of the Act, regarding any entry, matter or certificates.
thing that he is authorised or required by the Act or these Regulations
to make or do.

(2) A person who can show an interest in an entry, matter or thing
for which a certificate is required may, by an application in
Form No. 9, request the certificate from the Director, and the
applicant need not disclose his interest unless required by the Director
to do so.
(3) In a certificate issued under this provision the Director need
not include a copy of any design unless a suitable copy of the design
accompanies the application for the certificate.
38. The Director may acknowledge inquiries made to the Office,
Inquiries of
Office. but the Director need not furnish any applicants or other persons with
information that would require a search of the public records of the
Office or provide advice on matters concerning the interpretation of
the Act or Regulations or concerning other questions of law.
